claim:s3-protrusion-enclosure.proposition: Differential adhesion alone drives a deformable host to stable enclosure of a symbiont in a well-defined mechanical regime (J_hs below the J_sM - J_hM threshold); below the transition the host forms only a partial cup or leaves the symbiont free.
claim:s3-protrusion-enclosure.hypothesis: The host engulfs the symbiont when host-symbiont adhesion beats the combined surface-tension cost (J_hs < J_sM - J_hM); stable enclosure is the emergent plateau of the host's coverage of the symbiont boundary, with a sharp transition in the mechanical parameters.

primary_tests.name: Host reaches stable enclosure under strong adhesion

evidence_refs: Host reaches stable enclosure under strong adhesion
Weak adhesion leaves the symbiont free (failure route)

narrative.question: Can an archaeal-like deformable host physically surround and enclose a bacterial partner purely from differential adhesion, and under which mechanical conditions does wrapping reach a stable topology rather than a partial cup or a transient contact? This is the viva-cpm realization of gate G3 (Enclosure) of the viva-genesis eukaryogenesis campaign "The Endosymbiotic Transition" (campaign composite B — active membrane mechanics).
